items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: Mr. Hammond was the band master... Mr. Hammond asked me to come back to the band

ctx.x: Certainly you wouldn't have been in the service.

And now I hold a, not only a citation of honorable merit of the service, but a citation letter from my colonel. And the letter reads, a very valuable soldier to the United States Army. My best wishes go with you and I hope you will make a career of the service. And I could have made a career of the service because at that time there were four regular organized Negro regiments and I could have gone to any one of the bands at the request of their then band masters. And as early as the breakout of World War II, I…

I don't want to keep you more in a minute. I was trying to ask, when I was young, the only Negro band I ever heard of is the James Reese Europe band in the Army. Did yours compare? Was it anything bigger or special more than say the band like you had? Well, I don't try to be modest and say mine wasn't as good as this. I mean, actually in your opinion. That's right. Was your band in a class better or good?
